chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said:

We ate with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so they brought us meat from a slaughtered camel. I thought it was from his house, so we ate. Then they brought us a bowl of milk, and he drank from it. Then he said to me, 'Drink, O Abu Muhammad.' So I tasted it, and I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, milk!' He said, 'It is the nature (fitrah).' Then they brought us dates, and we ate them.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: The natural disposition or innate nature
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be a ransom for you (a common honorific phrase)
key_terms.لَحْمِ جَزُورٍ: Meat from a slaughtered animal (specifically camel here)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of milk in Shia dietary teachings according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly links the consumption of milk to *al-fitrah* (the primordial natural disposition), a concept central to Shia theology regarding human nature and divine guidance. This establishes dairy not merely as permissible food, but as a sustenance aligned with the innate purity and health of the human constitution, reinforcing the holistic view of diet in Islamic jurisprudence.
